name: SITT
description: In this work, we present the Social Influence Technique Taxonomy (SITT), a comprehensive framework of 58 empirically grounded techniques organized into nine categories, designed to detect subtle forms of social influence in textual content. We also investigated the LLMs' ability to identify various forms of social influence. Building on interdisciplinary foundations, we construct the SITT dataset - a 746-dialogue corpus annotated by 11 experts in Polish and translated into English - to evaluate the ability of LLMs to identify these techniques. Using a hierarchical multi-label classification setup, we benchmark five LLMs, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Llama-3.1, Mixtral, and PLLuM. Our results show that while some models, notably Claude 3.5, achieved moderate success (F1 score =0.45 for categories), the overall performance of the models remains limited, particularly for context-sensitive techniques.
